pack.name: The Vault Beneath the Ascendant Court
pack.description: Two rooms now: the vault proper (two dormant sentinels, two pillars, the Keeper) and, past the stairway the Keeper's death opens the way to, the reliquary the family letter was actually about.

pcOptions.name: Vesper Quill
pcOptions.title: Human Wizard 1
pcOptions.blurb: A scholar's approach: strike from range, close the fight with Breathe Fire and Force Fang, and lean on Shield when the resources run out. Fragile — 15 HP is a Keeper's fist and a half — but the widest toolkit in the vault.
pcOptions.paletteNote: The blue prism this game shipped with, kept for the build that was the only build.

pcOptions.name: Kessa Vane
pcOptions.title: Human Fighter 1
pcOptions.note: Expert proficiency +5 with the sword (level 1 + 4); the heirloom longsword in the satchel is finally being carried by someone who trained on one.
pcOptions.blurb: No spells, no tricks: three swings of the family longsword every turn and enough Hit Points to shrug off what the wizard cannot. Simpler than Vesper's list and, resource for resource, hits harder — the trade is a fixed plan with nothing held in reserve once the potions run out.
pcOptions.acNote: 10 + leather armor 1 + DEX 1 + Trained armor +2 (armor proficiency starts Trained even for a Fighter; weapon proficiency is the one that starts Expert) — measured light, not the heavier armor the class could wear, per balance.mjs (see note below)
pcOptions.paletteNote: Steel green, chosen against the board rather than for Kessa: the foes are red and the Keeper is purple, so a warm PC would read as one of them at a glance.
pcOptions.reactionsNote: No reactions modelled — same restraint as Vesper's Shield Block note. A Fighter's actual selling point (Attack of Opportunity) is exactly the priority-2 gap in the prompt, not something this build fakes with a wizard-shaped workaround.

commands.name: Strike — Dagger
commands.hint: Strike (◆): choose an adjacent sentinel. A critical hit leaves it clumsy.
commands.note: Finesse, so the +5 is DEX 2 + Trained 3, and "ability" is dex: the one attack in this pack not swung by Strength, which is what makes clumsy and enfeebled two conditions rather than the same one twice. Agile, so MAP is −4/−8 rather than −5/−10. The clumsy on a critical hit is this pack's own addition, not the dagger's. Clumsy 1 is −1 to the target's AC and Reflex save, which is Breathe Fire getting easier: the catalogue needed a source the player aims rather than only sources aimed at her.

commands.name: Strike — Longsword
commands.hint: Strike (◆): choose an adjacent creature. A critical hit leaves it enfeebled.
commands.note: STR 2 + Expert proficiency +5 (level 1 + 4) — Fighters start Expert with their trained weapon, unlike Vesper's Trained-only dagger. Not agile, so MAP is the standard −5/−10 rather than the dagger's −4/−8. STR 2, not the +4 a min-maxed build would carry — measured against balance.mjs, see the pcOptions note. The enfeebled on a critical hit is this pack's own addition: −1 to the target's Strength attacks and −1 off every point of weapon damage it deals, which is the first thing in this engine to move a damage roll from outside the weapon's own line. Kessa's answer to the dagger's clumsy. She has no spell whose DC a debuff can help, so hers takes the incoming number down instead.

commands.name: Shield
commands.hint: Shield (◆): a disc of force, +1 AC until your next turn begins.
commands.note: Player Core. The +1 is a circumstance bonus and lasts until the start of your next turn. Shield Block is not modelled — there are no reactions in this build.

commands.name: Rousing Splash
commands.hint: Rousing Splash (◆◆): a conjured wave crashes over you, and washes at any fire on you.
commands.note: Player Core p.409 lets a particularly appropriate action lower the flat check that ends persistent damage rather than end it outright, so this rolls DC 10 where the fire's own check is DC 15. Better odds, not a guarantee. It has something to end now: the Reliquary Warden's Cinder Fist sets the heir alight on a critical hit, and it is the only thing in the pack that puts persistent fire on the PC. The note this replaces described a rule written for a game that did not exist.

commands.name: Breathe Fire
commands.hint: Breathe Fire (◆◆, spends a rank-1 slot): click a direction — 15-ft cone, basic Reflex DC 17. A critical failure catches fire.
commands.note: Burning Hands was renamed Breathe Fire in the Remaster. Implemented under its legal name. The persistent fire on a critical failure is this pack's own addition, not the spell's: the Remaster spell leaves nothing behind. It is here because a condition system with nothing in the adventure that applies one is a system nobody plays, and a basic save that already rolls four degrees is the cheapest honest place to hang the fourth. Measured, not guessed — see the balance numbers in the phase handoff.

commands.name: Ember Burst
commands.hint: Ember Burst (◆◆, spends a rank-1 slot): click a square within 30 ft — a 10-foot burst, basic Reflex DC 17.
commands.note: This pack's own rank-1 spell rather than one lifted from a book, flagged here the way Force Fang's departure is. It exists because the burst template needed one command to ship exercised, and the cone could not be that command: a cone starts at the heir, so the only way to catch two sentinels in one is to let both of them reach her. A burst is placed, and thirty feet of placement is what makes it worth a slot. Weaker per creature than Breathe Fire on purpose — 1d6 against 2d6 — and drawn from the same two slots, so what it adds to the delve is a question about the shape of the room rather than more magic.

commands.name: Warding Pulse
commands.hint: Warding Pulse (◆): a ring of the seal's own gold snaps out ten feet from where you stand — basic Reflex DC 17, everything it touches.
commands.note: The emanation template's one command, and a cantrip rather than a slot spell because an emanation is centred on the caster: it only pays once a construct has already closed on a 15 HP wizard, which is exactly when she cannot afford to have spent a slot on the hope that one would. Its case is that a basic save rolls no attack and so takes no multiple attack penalty — she leads with the dagger and follows with the ring, because the swing the ring displaces is the one at −4. One action, not two, and that was decided by the action economy rather than by taste: a three-action turn against something in reach is Strike, ring, disc, and a two-action ring leaves no room for the disc at all. Shipped at a flat 1d4 and measured against the alternative over 2,000 seeded runs per build — 1d4 puts the heir at 82.8%, 1d4+2 at 86.7%, and the band's ceiling is 90%. This pack's own spell, same departure as Ember Burst and the same reason.

commands.name: Force Fang
commands.hint: Force Fang (◆, 1 Focus): click a sentinel within 30 ft — no attack roll, unerring force, and it pins what it hits.
commands.note: Strictly a Magus focus spell (Secrets of Magic). Kept per the original design spec; it behaves like Magic Missile. The slowed 1 is this pack's own addition and the only source of slowed in it: a fang of force through the joint costs a construct one of its three actions until the end of its next turn. It is on an unerring command on purpose, because slowed is the one condition worth a whole focus point and an attack roll would make it a coin flip. Vesper has one focus point for the entire delve, so it fires at most once a run.

commands.name: Drink Healing Potion
commands.note: Interact. The potion is treated as already drawn, so drawing it does not cost a second action.

commands.name: Gravel Wave
commands.hint: Gravel Wave (◆◆): the Keeper drives a fist into the floor and fifteen feet of it comes up at you.
commands.note: Nobody's build lists this, so no heir can cast it: it is in the shared command list because a creature's abilities are looked up there, the same way its reactions are. It carries its own DC 16 — a moderate DC for a level-0 creature — rather than borrowing the heir's spell DC, which is what stops a stupefied Vesper from making a construct's floor easier to dodge. Once per encounter, and 2 actions of a 3-action turn, so the round it goes off is a round with one Basalt Fist in it instead of two. Measured against the alternative rather than guessed: two Fists at +4 into AC 15 average about 4.1 damage, and 2d6 basic Reflex at DC 16 averages about 3.9 with no attack roll to miss with, so the wave is the opener and the second Fist is what it displaces. A critical failure leaves the heir off-guard, which is the sentinels' own crit rider arriving a room early and from the floor rather than the fist.

commands.name: Reactive Strike
commands.hint: Reactive Strike (↺): fires by itself when something leaves your reach. It is not a button.
commands.note: Attack of Opportunity was renamed Reactive Strike in the Remaster, and Fighters have it at 1st level. Implemented under its legal name, the way Breathe Fire is. Kessa's longsword numbers: +7 and 1d8+2, with no multiple-attack penalty taken and none added, because the swing happens on somebody else's turn and MAP belongs to your own. A creature that lists this strikes with its own attack instead — a basalt fist is not a longsword whichever feat swings it.

commands.name: Shield Block
commands.hint: Shield Block (↺): while Shield is up, the disc soaks 5 physical damage and is spent doing it.
commands.note: Player Core. The Shield cantrip's force disc has Hardness 5 and can Shield Block; blocking destroys it, so the +1 AC goes with it. Physical damage only — the disc does nothing about fire. It fires without asking, because the disc lapses at the start of your next turn either way: declining it only wastes it.

shattered-sentinel.name: Shattered Sentinel
shattered-sentinel.deathLine: {name} shatters into gravel and gold dust.
shattered-sentinel.wakeLine: Rubble shudders upright into a humanoid shape — {name} still keeps its post.
shattered-sentinel.sleepLine: {name} loses you in the dark. The rubble settles, and reknits.
shattered-sentinel.note: Creature -1 on GM Core's Building Creatures benchmarks, and Low on every line except Fortitude: HP 11, AC 13, attack +4, damage 1d6, Fort +5 high because it is masonry, Will +0 low because it does not think. 10 XP each against a solo level-1 PC. The binding constraint is not the statline, it is that a level-1 wizard has two spell slots and one focus point for the whole delve — see the note on vault-keeper. The off-guard on a critical hit is this pack's own addition: a fist of masonry puts the heir on the back foot, and she recovers it at the start of her next turn. Off-guard is a −2 circumstance penalty to AC, which is the first circumstance penalty in the pack and the reason Vesper's disc is worth casting into it rather than instead of it: a bonus and a penalty both apply whether or not they share a type, so the disc still buys its point back.

vault-keeper.name: The Vault Keeper
vault-keeper.deathLine: The Keeper kneels, and does not rise. Gold dust settles over the casket.
vault-keeper.wakeLine: The shape beside the casket was never rubble. {name} stands, and the chamber narrows.
vault-keeper.note: A critical Basalt Fist leaves the heir frightened 1 and stupefied 1 — the wake line already says the chamber narrows, and this is that sentence with a number on it. Frightened 1 is a −1 status penalty to every check and to AC, wearing off at the end of the heir's own turn, so it costs one turn of arithmetic rather than a spiral. Stupefied 1 is −1 to her spell DC and a DC 6 flat check on every spell she casts until the end of her next turn, which is the only place in this engine a condition costs a caster the spell rather than a number. It costs Kessa nothing at all, because she casts nothing, and that is the clearest reading this pack has of how differently the two builds feel one fist. The statline the two sentinels originally shipped with (17 HP, AC 14, fist +6 for 1d6+2), promoted to the boss it was always sized for: 15 XP against a solo level-1 PC, and the only fight the PC arrives at with a full spell list, because opening the gate restores them. The number was never wrong; it was pointed at the wrong fight, twice over.

reliquary-warden.name: Reliquary Warden
reliquary-warden.deathLine: {name} folds at the joints and does not rise again.
reliquary-warden.wakeLine: A last construct rises between you and the reliquary — {name}.
reliquary-warden.sleepLine: {name} loses you in the dark and settles back to stone.
reliquary-warden.note: Deliberately weaker than either sentinel (8 HP vs 11, AC 12 vs 13, +3 vs +4, 1d4 vs 1d6): the PC reaches it with whatever the Keeper fight left. Measured both ways over 2000 seeded runs: at full sentinel stats this creature measures 41.5% wins, just under the 45% floor; at these numbers it measures 53.6%. Neither is a small effect — a fourth mandatory fight moves the needle even weakened well below sentinel strength. Its fist carries the reliquary's own ward: fire rather than bludgeoning, and a critical hit sets the heir alight for 1d4 a turn until a DC 15 flat check puts it out. It is the only thing in the pack that puts persistent fire on the PC, which is what gives Rousing Splash something to end, and Shield Block cannot soak it because the disc does nothing about fire and says so.

startingInventoryNote: Three Minor Healing Potions, not two. A solo level-1 wizard's entire day is two spell slots and one focus point; potions are the only resource that can be bought rather than rested for, and the balance harness says the delve needs about thirteen points of them.

bequest.title: The Western Pillar — The Bequest
body: Chisel-work in pre-Absalom Kelish, gold leaf still bright in the grooves:
"I, Sarvel of the First Landing, leave what I carried up from the sea to the heir with wit enough to find it. The city above will grow fat and forgetful. Let this vault stay lean and patient."
A recess below the text is shaped like half of a two-piece seal.
bequest.logLine: You study the western pillar. Old words, older intent.

condition.title: The Eastern Pillar — The Condition
body: The same hand, generations older, the letters shakier:
"The sentinels do not guard the gold. They guard the question: will the heir read both stones before forcing the gate? Patience was ever the family's rarest coin."
The second half of the seal glows faintly as you finish reading. Somewhere ahead, stone grinds against stone.
condition.logLine: You study the eastern pillar. Old words, older intent.

reliquary.title: The Reliquary Plaque
body: Newer stonework than the pillars below, and blunter: "Sarvel's heir: the sentinels were the test. The Keeper was the price. What is past both is only ever yours if you can still lift it."
Beneath the text, a mason's mark rather than a seal — this room was cut after the vault, not with it.
reliquary.logLine: You read the reliquary plaque. Whoever finished this room came after Sarvel, and knew exactly what they were guarding.

vault.name: The Vault Beneath the Ascendant Court

sanctum.name: The Reliquary
sanctum.hint: The reliquary. The casket is behind the warden — there is no way back up the stair.

gate.sealedHint: The gate is sealed by a two-part sigil. Perhaps the pillars…
gate.sealedLog: The gate does not move. Two empty seal-recesses flank it.
gate.openNarrative: Both halves of the seal flare gold. The gate's counterweights release — the way north stands open.
gate.restoreNarrative: The seal's release washes back down the stair. Bruises fade, your prepared spells settle into place again, and the focus you spent returns.
gate.restoreNote: This is the adventure's only rest, and it is what makes two acts out of one room. Everything the sentinels cost you comes back except potions, which is the point: potions are the currency the delve is actually played in, and a player who slips past a sentinel using the wall blocks as cover arrives at the Keeper holding all three.
gate.openHint: The gate is open. The Inheritance waits beyond.

treasure.blockedHint: Something still stands between you and the casket lid.
treasure.title: The Absalom Inheritance
body: Inside the casket: a founder's deed, sealed the day the Starstone fell — title to a sliver of the Ascendant Court itself, made out to whichever heir could pass the sentinels and read the pillars true.
You are, as of this moment, minor landed gentry of Absalom. The paperwork will take decades.

defeat.title: Dying — the Vault Keeps Its Secret
body: Vesper falls at 0 HP and gains the dying 1 condition. With no ally to Administer First Aid, the ruin reclaims its silence.
Full dying and recovery-check rules are out of scope for this vignette — a rules-lawyer confession.

intro.narrative: Beneath the Ascendant Court, the family letter led you true: a vault older than the Starstone Cathedral, air thick with rock dust and patience.
intro.goal: Read both pillars to open the northern gate, then take the stairway beyond it to the reliquary and claim the Inheritance. A sentinel wakes if you stray within 30 ft of it and it can see you.
intro.hint: Click a lit tile to walk, or use the arrow keys. Approach the carved pillars to read them.
